document_check.note: The document is Ponirakis et al., 'Corneal nerve loss predicts dementia in patients with mild cognitive impairment', Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology 2023;10(4):599-609. It is a longitudinal memory-clinic cohort from Qatar with 107 MCI participants, 33 of whom progressed to dementia, and it reports corneal nerve measures as predictors of progression, as the review cites.

cited_result: The association of baseline corneal nerve loss (corneal confocal microscopy) with progression from MCI to dementia over a median 2.4 years. Principal result: abnormal CNFD (≤25/mm2) has an adjusted OR of 6.1 (95% CI 1.6-23.8); supporting results are an adjusted OR of 4.1 (1.2-14.2) for abnormal CNBD and AUC 74% for CNFD.
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of a single prognostic factor (corneal nerve integrity) with later progression to dementia; no multivariable prediction model is developed or validated.

domains.rationale: The source clinic, period and exclusions are described. The sampling method (consecutive or not) and the participation rate are not reported. MCI was defined by ICD-10 F06.7 without biomarkers, and half of the cohort reverted to normal cognition, which suggests some baseline misclassification.

signalling.question: Adequate participation in the study by eligible persons
signalling.quote: Searched for the number of eligible or approached people, participation rate, and 'consecutive' or 'random' sampling. Only the number enrolled (130 with MCI) is reported.

signalling.question: Description of the source population, sampling frame, period and place of recruitment
signalling.quote: In this longitudinal cohort study, individuals with no cognitive impairment (NCI) and MCI aged 60–85 years were recruited from the geriatric and memory clinic in Rumailah Hospital, Qatar from 2016–2020

signalling.question: Description of the baseline study sample
signalling.quote: Comparison of clinical characteristics, cognitive function, corneal confocal microscopy measures and MRI brain volumetry between patients with mild cognitive impairment who did and did not progress to dementia.

signalling.question: Adequate description of inclusion and exclusion criteria
signalling.quote: Exclusion criteria applied by geriatricians, geriatric psychiatrists and neurologists were dementia, Parkinson’s disease, severe anxiety, severe depression, mood disorders, psychosis, hypomania [...] The diagnosis of MCI was based on ICD-10: F06.7 criteria version: 2019.

domains.rationale: 23 of 130 enrolled participants (18%) were not analysed: 3 dropped out and 20 had follow-up shorter than 12 months. Reasons are given, but those not analysed are not described or compared with those analysed.

signalling.question: Adequate response rate and reasons for loss to follow-up provided
signalling.quote: 3 dropped out due to incomplete assessments, and 20 were not included in the analysis as their follow-up assessments were <12-months from enrolment

signalling.question: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
signalling.quote: Searched for any follow-up of the 3 drop-outs or the 20 excluded for short follow-up. None was described.

signalling.question: Description of those lost, and no important differences between completers and non-completers
signalling.quote: Searched for a comparison of baseline characteristics or CCM values between the 107 analysed and the 23 not analysed. None was reported.

domains.rationale: CCM was acquired with one device for everyone, images were selected by an investigator blinded to diagnosis, cognition and MRI, and nerves were quantified manually with CCMetrics. However, the 'abnormal' cut-off (CNFD ≤25/mm2) was derived from the same data with Youden's index and then used as the exposure for the adjusted OR, so the cut-point is data-dependent and the OR is optimistic.

signalling.question: A clear definition or description of the prognostic factor is provided
signalling.quote: The central cornea was selected for imaging the sub-basal nerve plexus.

signalling.question: Method of prognostic factor measurement is adequately valid and reliable
signalling.quote: by an investigator who was blinded from the diagnosis, cognitive function, and MRI brain volumetry [...] were measured manually using CCMetrics

signalling.question: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate (not data-dependent) cut-points are used
signalling.quote: the cut-off value with optimal discriminative power for sensitivity [...] The OR for progression to dementia after adjusting for age, MoCA, hypertension, triglycerides, HDL and diabetes duration remained 6.1 (95% CI: 1.6–23.8) times higher with abnormal CNFD

signalling.question: Method and setting of measurement is the same for all participants
signalling.quote: CCM analysis was performed in both eyes

signalling.question: Adequate proportion of the sample has complete prognostic factor data
signalling.quote: Participants unable to cooperate during the CCM assessments were also excluded.

domains.rationale: Dementia was diagnosed by ICD-10 criteria at routine clinic visits rather than by a standardised research assessment. Follow-up length varied from 1 to 4.5 years, and blinding of diagnosing clinicians to CCM is not reported. The 50.5% reversion rate points to instability in the clinical classification.

signalling.question: A clear definition of the outcome is provided
signalling.quote: The diagnosis of dementia, including AD, vascular dementia (VaD) and mixed AD was based on ICD-10

signalling.question: Method of outcome measurement is adequately valid and reliable (including blinding to the prognostic factor)
signalling.quote: CCM and brain MRI assessments were performed at baseline only and the follow-up was undertaken in a routine clinic visit. [Searched for blinding of the diagnosing clinicians to CCM results; none reported.]

signalling.question: Method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all participants
signalling.quote: were completed in 20 (19%) participants within 1–2 years, 35 (32%) participants within 2–3 years, 29 (27%) participants within 3–4 years, and 23 (22%) participants within 4–5 years of their baseline assessment

domains.rationale: Plausible confounders were measured and the final model adjusts for age, MoCA, hypertension, triglycerides, HDL and diabetes duration. The covariates were chosen by bivariate p ≤ 0.05 rather than on conceptual grounds. Diabetes, which causes corneal nerve loss, enters only as duration, and the paper does not say how duration was coded for participants without diabetes.

signalling.question: All important confounders are measured
signalling.quote: the independent variables were abnormal corneal nerve measures or abnormal brain volumetry, age, sex, MoCA, education level, sleep deprivation, diabetes, duration of diabetes, obesity, hypertension, total cholesterol, triglyceride, HDL, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, weight, and BMI

signalling.question: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis
signalling.quote: The OR for progression to dementia after adjusting for age, MoCA, hypertension, triglycerides, HDL and diabetes duration remained 6.1 (95% CI: 1.6–23.8) times higher with abnormal CNFD

signalling.question: Appropriate handling of missing or undefined confounder data
signalling.quote: Diabetes was not excluded as it is highly prevalent in patients attending the clinic. [Searched for how duration of diabetes was coded for non-diabetic participants and how many were in the adjusted model; not reported.]

domains.rationale: A binary logistic model treats participants with 1 year of follow-up the same as those with 4.5 years, so short follow-up is counted as non-progression; there is no time-to-event analysis, and the authors acknowledge the limitation. There are about 33 events for 7 parameters, covariates were selected by bivariate significance, and listwise deletion was used without reporting the analysed number. The abstract claims CCM has higher prognostic accuracy than volumetry, although AUCs favour hippocampal and whole-brain volume (78% vs 74%); the claim rests on Youden-threshold accuracy.

signalling.question: Sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis
signalling.quote: Since listwise missing was used in this prior logistic regression

signalling.question: Strategy for model building is appropriate and based on a conceptual framework
signalling.quote: Variables with p ≤0.05 at the bivariate level were included in the multiple logistic regression.

signalling.question: Selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study
signalling.quote: In the binary logistic regression analysis, the dependent variables were progression from MCI to dementia [...] the wide follow-up range of 1–4.5 years may limit accurate evaluation of the predictive capability of CCM

signalling.question: No selective reporting of results
signalling.quote: However, CCM had a higher prognostic accuracy (72%–75% vs 68%–69%) for identifying individuals who progressed to dementia compared to hippocampus and whole brain volume.

overall: High risk of bias (QUIPS: domain 6 high; domains 1 to 5 moderate)
overall_rationale: Domain 6 is high because a binary logistic model with few events per parameter ignores follow-up that ranged from 1 to 4.5 years, and covariates were chosen by data-driven selection. Each of domains 1 to 5 has moderate concerns: unreported sampling and ICD-10 MCI with 50.5% reversion; 18% not analysed and not compared; a data-derived cut-off used as the exposure; routine-clinic outcome ascertainment without reported blinding; and bivariate-p confounder selection. Under the QUIPS rule, any high domain or three or more moderate domains gives overall high risk.

applicability.rationale: A single memory clinic in Qatar where 51% of MCI participants had diabetes. MCI was defined by ICD-10 F06.7 rather than Petersen or NIA-AA criteria.
All-cause dementia (AD, vascular and mixed) diagnosed at routine clinic visits, with no biomarker confirmation.
